slides.purpose: Frame extensions as responses to worked obstructions under preservation constraints.
slides.successCheck: Reader names a failed question and asks what must remain unchanged.

slides.purpose: Declare the natural-number convention and distinguish two roles of zero.
slides.successCheck: Reader states ℕ={0,1,2,…} as a convention and separates empty count from additive identity.

slides.purpose: Work 2−5 and expose failure of closure in ℕ.
slides.successCheck: Reader traces five equal left steps to −3 and states the repair requirement.

slides.purpose: Repair subtraction with additive inverses while preserving earlier arithmetic.
slides.successCheck: Reader reconstructs 2−5=2+(−5)=−3 and explains what is preserved.

slides.purpose: Show that the integer repair does not solve 2x=1.
slides.successCheck: Reader connects equal sharing to a multiplicative inverse and excludes denominator zero.

slides.purpose: Treat fractions as representations of values rather than unique names.
slides.successCheck: Reader verifies 1/2=2/4 by cross-products and embeds n as n/1.

slides.purpose: Derive 1/2+1/3 from a common unit.
slides.successCheck: Reader obtains 5/6 and explains why numerator-and-denominator addition changes the unit.

slides.purpose: Expose an exact geometric length outside ℚ.
slides.successCheck: Reader derives d²=2 and separates approximation, existence, and irrationality.

slides.purpose: Separate fine rational interpolation from boundary inclusion.
slides.successCheck: Reader distinguishes rational midpoint density, ℚ-density in ℝ, and least-upper-bound completeness.

slides.purpose: State the least-upper-bound goal with its ambient universe and hypotheses.
slides.successCheck: Reader distinguishes upper bound, least upper bound, and maximum, and does not substitute Cauchy completeness by name alone.

slides.purpose: Show the algebraic obstruction x²=−1 inside ordered real arithmetic.
slides.successCheck: Reader closes the positive, negative, and zero sign cases and identifies the new goal.

slides.purpose: Construct i²=−1 while preserving real operations through ordered pairs.
slides.successCheck: Reader computes i² and (1,1)(1,−1) directly from pair multiplication.

slides.purpose: Interpret multiplication by i through one exact coordinate example.
slides.successCheck: Reader maps (2,−1) to (1,2), checks equal squared lengths, and handles zero separately.

slides.purpose: Answer the opening with a property ledger rather than a largest-system claim.
slides.successCheck: Reader names one repair and one constraint at every transition.

slides.purpose: Make the nonzero-denominator domain part of the quotient construction.
slides.successCheck: Reader reproduces the (0,0) counterexample to transitivity of the naively enlarged relation.

slides.purpose: Prove transitivity without presupposing rational division.
slides.successCheck: Reader derives d(af−be)=0 and uses d≠0 for integer cancellation.

slides.purpose: Start the irrationality contradiction from a reduced fraction.
slides.successCheck: Reader derives p²=2q² and p=2k while preserving the separate existence assumption.

slides.purpose: Complete the second parity branch.
slides.successCheck: Reader proves q is even and identifies the contradiction with gcd(p,q)=1.

slides.purpose: Make the ambient ordered universe control eligible bounds.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains why √2 is eligible in ℝ but not ℚ and why it need not be a maximum.

slides.purpose: Eliminate every rational least-upper-bound candidate.
slides.successCheck: Reader handles r≤0, 0<r<√2, r=√2, and r>√2 without skipping a case.

slides.purpose: Derive the Archimedean constraint from the least-upper-bound property.
slides.successCheck: Reader obtains s<n+1 from s=sup ℕ and states the contradiction.

slides.purpose: Give a reconstructable proof sketch of complete-ordered-field uniqueness.
slides.successCheck: Reader defines the rational cut map, explains injectivity and surjectivity, and says isomorphism is not literal identity.

slides.purpose: Answer the larger-system question with a concrete non-Archimedean ordered field.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains why t>n for all n and which complete-ordered-field condition therefore fails.

slides.purpose: Prove the exact order structure unavailable on ℂ.
slides.successCheck: Reader closes both i>0 and −i>0 branches without banning arbitrary comparisons.

slides.purpose: Compare the property bundles selected by real and complex extensions.
slides.successCheck: Reader states the hypotheses needed for real-field uniqueness and the algebraic gain/order cost of ℂ.
